messages.author: 1d0e5ccd9786d9de
messages.subject: Problem getting started with ArrayExplorer
parts:
Hello,
I am just getting started using aroma.affymetrix, so I am trying to
run through a basic analysis of a set of HG-U133_Plus_2 arrays using
code I've collected from this group. My problem comes with trying to
display residual plots using ArrayExplorer - I get an ArrayExplorer
page (in Firefox 2.0.0.12) with a correct listing of file names, but
the display region simply shows a greatly enlarged copy of the
animated 'indicator.gif' image. Am I doing something obviously wrong?
I tried disabling all Firefox add-ons, which had no effect. Thanks for
any help...
Michael

Here's the relevant code:

library(EBImage)
library(aroma.affymetrix)
library(affyPLM)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "Project"
chipType <- "HG-U133_Plus_2"

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)

setCdf(cs, cdf)

# RMA background correction
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs);
csBC <- process(bc, verbose=verbose);

# RMA quantile normalization
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm");
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose);

# RMA probe summarization
plm <- RmaPlm(csN);
fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
rs <- calculateResidualSet(plm)

ae <- ArrayExplorer(rs)
setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,log2neg,rainbow", "log2,log2pos,rainbow"))
process(ae, interleaved="auto")
display(ae)

On Tue, Mar 25, 2008 at 10:21 AM, michael <Michael...@fccc.edu> wrote:
>
> Hello,
> I am just getting started using aroma.affymetrix, so I am trying to
> run through a basic analysis of a set of HG-U133_Plus_2 arrays using
> code I've collected from this group. My problem comes with trying to
> display residual plots using ArrayExplorer - I get an ArrayExplorer
> page (in Firefox 2.0.0.12) with a correct listing of file names, but
> the display region simply shows a greatly enlarged copy of the
> animated 'indicator.gif' image. Am I doing something obviously wrong?
> I tried disabling all Firefox add-ons, which had no effect. Thanks for
> any help...
> Michael

You have found a bug that was introduced in aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0
causing the ArrayExplorer (actually a helper class) to output the
images in a directory that has replicated tags. For instance, in your
case the PNG files should have been saved to:

reports/Project/RBC,QN,RMA/HG-U133_Plus_2/spatial/

but they ended up in:

reports/Project/RBC,QN,RMA,RBC,QN,RMA/HG-U133_Plus_2/spatial/

If you move those PNG files in the 2nd path to the first path, the
ArrayExplorer should display the plots as expected.

I have committed a patch that fixes the above. To install the patch, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

More comments about your script below.

>
> Here's the relevant code:
>
> library(EBImage)
> library(aroma.affymetrix)
> library(affyPLM)
>
> verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
> timestampOn(verbose)
> name <- "Project"
> chipType <- "HG-U133_Plus_2"
>
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
>
> setCdf(cs, cdf)

FYI, you do not have to setup the 'cdf' and call setCdf() here; the
default CDF is set by default and it is only when you use a custom CDF
when you have to do that.

Cheers

/Henrik

>
> # RMA background correction
> bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs);
> csBC <- process(bc, verbose=verbose);
>
> # RMA quantile normalization
> qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm");
> csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose);
>
> # RMA probe summarization
> plm <- RmaPlm(csN);
> fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
> rs <- calculateResidualSet(plm)
>
> ae <- ArrayExplorer(rs)
> setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,log2neg,rainbow", "log2,log2pos,rainbow"))
> process(ae, interleaved="auto")
> display(ae)
>
